rules.note: Ballotage: a candidate wins in the first round with more than 45% of the vote, or with 40% and a lead of more than 10 points over the runner-up; otherwise the top two meet in a run-off. The game's default two-round rule uses an absolute majority, so first-round wins with between 45% and 50% (2007, 2019) rely on the historical record. One consecutive re-election.
Half of the Chamber (127 or 130 seats) is renewed every two years for four-year terms.
One third of the Senate (eight provinces, 24 seats) is renewed every two years for six-year terms; all 72 seats were elected in 2001.

historical.note: seats = chamber composition after the election from the results table's Total column; seats_won = seats won (127 contested). Shares are the infobox percentages of the blocs' lists. Fronts are recorded under their leading party: Front for Victory, Citizen's Unity, Frente de Todos, Union for the Homeland and Homeland Force under arg.pj; Social and Civic Agreement, Union for Social Development and the Progressive, Civic and Social Front under arg.ucr; Cambiemos/Juntos por el Cambio and (2009) Federal Peronism-PRO Union under arg.pro; United for a New Alternative and 1País under arg.fr; Broad Progressive Front and Progresistas under arg.ps; 'Libertarians' (2021) under arg.lla.

historical.note: Shares of valid votes computed from the results table (alliance totals). Menem (Front for Loyalty), Kirchner (Front for Victory) and Adolfo Rodríguez Saá (Front of the Popular Movement) were all Peronists running on separate fronts. No candidate reached 45%, but Menem withdrew before the run-off scheduled for May, so Kirchner became President. Others: Leopoldo Moreau (UCR) 2.34% and minor candidates.
